dialect.detail: Generic COBOL-85 style; uses EVALUATE/END-EVALUATE and inline PERFORM with END-PERFORM. The 'FILE NAME IS FileName' clause on OPEN OUTPUT is non-standard and may not compile on most compilers without extensions.
evidence: AT END / NOT AT END in READ
OPEN OUTPUT StudentFile FILE NAME IS FileName

purpose.domain_detail: Student information management demo illustrating file handling concepts
purpose.summary: A simple student information program that opens a text file, allows the user to add student records (name and number) or view the list, and exits on demand. It demonstrates basic COBOL file I/O, EVALUATE, and PERFORM constructs.

notable_features: Dynamic file name via ACCEPT into FileName used in OPEN (non-standard FILE NAME IS clause)
WRITE...AFTER ADVANCING used for sequential output
READ with AT END / NOT AT END inline handlers
EVALUATE with WHEN OTHER for menu dispatch
No ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / SELECT / ASSIGN clause present (unusual for file handling)
verdict.notes: The ENVIRONMENT DIVISION is absent, meaning there is no SELECT/ASSIGN clause for StudentFile, which is required by standard COBOL. The 'FILE NAME IS FileName' on the OPEN statement is non-standard and likely would not compile as-is on most COBOL compilers. This appears to be a student exercise or tutorial example illustrating file handling concepts rather than runnable production code.
